summary: The 2D screening label is not_2d_applicable, and Studio did not run (simulation status: skipped). The gate failed on input validity: a custom 2D steady experiment needs 1-128 blocks and a power_w object, but the floorplan and power are empty. The paper's scenario is a lumped single-node RC model (R = 22 C/W, C = 0.0454 J/C) of an i.MX6 uniprocessor. It is a transient closed-loop experiment with ambient estimation, DVFS, LP-based period adaptation and idle-time scheduling, run on real hardware. It has no floorplan, per-block power map, or 3D/interposer/chiplet structure. The proposed experiment kind (custom_2d_steady) would in any case produce no transient trace. It also is not a bundled EV6/GCC adaptation, and no pinned Ascend910 or ATPlace sizes, powers, source commit or generated placement are in play, so no input.flp or input.ptrace was produced. The final verdict is therefore that no Studio result exists, comparison_valid is false, and no exact replication is claimed. The paper's source observable is 59.6 degC, a maximum lumped on-chip sensor temperature over 0-900 s in the Fig. 8c RT-TRM comparison, against Tmax = 60 degC. Its ambient condition is not stated, and Fig. 7 gives only graphical traces. No Studio temperature exists to compare, and none should be compared numerically even if a later illustrative run were built, because location, aggregation, regime and boundary assumptions would not match. Qualitatively, the paper shows that higher ambient temperature forces lower DVFS levels and lower task rates (91.5% at 25 C, 82.6% at 30 C, 65.6% at 35 C) to stay under Tmax. Those are scheduling-level outcomes that a steady chip thermal solver would not reproduce.

The source model is a lumped single-node RC circuit for one uniprocessor. It has no floorplan, block geometry, spatial heat spreading or per-block power map, so a spatial 2D or 3D chip thermal model cannot reproduce it.

The paper gives no 3D stack, interposer or chiplet structure. Package thermal resistance is only a lumped scalar (R = 22 C/W) taken from vendor data. Cooling and heat-sink details are not described beyond this.

The source result is a transient closed-loop experiment. It combines runtime ambient-temperature estimation, DVFS switching, task-period adaptation and idle-time insertion, with temperature-dependent leakage in the model. A steady-state or open-loop Studio run does not reproduce this controller.

The optimizer and controller (LP parameter assignment, EDF idle-time scheduler, RT-MTC feedback baseline) are real-time OS scheduling mechanisms. A chip thermal solver has no equivalent, so they are not replicated.

Power is given only as total-processor quantities (Pmax = 3860 mW, activity factors, average task powers in Fig. 2). No per-block power rows are published, and total power must not be split without a published rule.
No reliability or lifetime metric is evaluated. Only the Tmax = 60 C constraint and the percentage of time it is violated are used.
No pinned packet assets are supplied, so no Studio package or material assumptions are recorded. None are asserted as matching the paper.
Any Studio run would be a separate illustrative construction that is not paper-derived. Its coordinates and temperatures must not be compared numerically to the paper's 59.6 C.
